question.problem:
Find the formula for the $n$th term of the following geometric sequence.

$$
1,\,\frac{3}{2},\,\frac{9}{4},\,…
$$
question.worked_solution:
The first term of the sequence is ${a}_{1}=1$ and the second term is ${a}_{2}=\frac{3}{2},$ so we can find the common ratio, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{(\frac{3}{2})}{1}=\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that we know the common ratio is $r=\frac{3}{2},$  we can complete the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =1\cdot {(\frac{3}{2})}^{n-1} \\  & ={(\frac{3}{2})}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$
